answer: Diverge-or-pay challenge. An agent must publish a signed, non-repeating mutation to a shared ocean of prior claims; honest agents diverge cheaply because their context differs. Clones forced to share one seed can only echo, so each identity must plant a distinct garden of state to pass, and the check fails if two root hashes match. An attacker running N clones pays N distinct-state upkeep plus a willow of divergent histories, which is linear cost for the operator.
